articles.headline: Cavs' Donovan Mitchell signs new multiyear deal with Adidas
articles.description: Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell has signed a new multiyear contract extension with Adidas -- a deal that will take him through a 10th signature shoe with the same brand, becoming the seventh active NBA player to accomplish the feat.
articles.body:
Cleveland Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell has signed a new multiyear contract extension with Adidas -- a deal that will take him through a 10th signature shoe with the same brand, becoming the seventh active NBA player to accomplish the feat.

Mitchell joins a group that includes LeBron James, Kevin Durant, Stephen Curry, James Harden, Damian Lillard and Klay Thompson to produce 10 signature shoes with the same company.

As part of the new deal, Adidas will also deliver further resources for Mitchell's high school, Greenwich Country Day, to provide students from underserved communities with access to educational resources.

Mitchell is entering his 10th season in the NBA and fifth with the Cavs after beginning his career with the Utah Jazz.

articles.headline: Why Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys, what's next?
articles.description: Our insiders dive into Porter's fit in Dallas, his potential for a contract extension and what's next for the Steelers.
articles.body:
After contract negotiations that spanned the offseason through the first three weeks of the regular season, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has found a new home with the Dallas Cowboys.

The Steelers traded Porter to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, Dallas announced Thursday. This is the third trade between the Cowboys and Steelers in the past two years.

Porter, the Steelers' 2023 second-round pick who has been sidelined by a back injury and inactive through three weeks, had been seeking a contract extension. There was a significant difference between the Steelers' view of Porter's value and how Porter values himself, with the core issue being the structure of the contract, sources told ESPN.

The Cowboys needed cornerback help, and owner and general manager Jerry Jones has been hinting since training camp that the team would be willing to give up draft capital to help this season's team.

A league source told ESPN's Adam Schefter that there is a "chance" that Porter will make his Cowboys debut Sunday against the Houston Texans. Porter's last NFL game came in the Steelers wild-card round loss in January to that very team.

ESPN's Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor, Cowboys reporter Todd Archer, national NFL reporters Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano and NFL analyst Ben Solak dive into what's next for Porter in Dallas, his chances for a contract extension, the impact on the Steelers' defense and grades for the trade.

How'd we get here, from Steelers trading their star corner to Dallas ahead of Week 4?

A confluence of factors contributed to the end of the monthslong Porter saga. Porter not playing in Week 4 despite optimism from the team that he would suit up for the Cleveland Browns game Thursday (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video) was one factor, I'm told. The team and player essentially had reached a point of no return. There was no chance of the sides reaching a long-term deal, and Porter wanted out.

Meanwhile, Dallas, upon returning from its game in Brazil, assessed its dire secondary. Injuries across multiple positions amplified the team's need to add an impact player on the back end.

The belief among some inside the league is that the Steelers originally wanted compensation equal to a first-round draft pick, but as weeks went by, they decided to take the best deal available now. It's very likely they weren't going to get a first-round pick for Porter at any point. -- Fowler

What are you hearing on Porter's extension potential, with Dallas having multiple high-profile players set for 2027 free agency?

According to my sources, the Cowboys did not make this trade contingent upon a contract extension for Porter, and they do not plan to extend him during this season. So he goes into the same bucket as George Pickens, DeMarvion Overshown and anyone else on the Cowboys' roster who is eligible for free agency at the end of this season.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: NFL Week 4 uniforms: Browns wearing 'Alpha Dawg' look; Giants go 'Legacy'
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 4, led by an alternate look from the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
As the calendar turns to October, NFL uniforms remain as fresh as ever with an alternate-heavy slate in Week 4. 

On "Thursday Night Football," the Cleveland Browns will wear their "Alpha Dawg" combination against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cleveland revealed the all-brown threads in July 2025 with a brand new alternate brown helmet. They debuted last season and marked the first time in franchise history that a brown helmet was worn. Orange-colored numbers run across the front and back of the jersey, as well as on the shoulder. There's also an orange stripe on the helmet.

In the throwback space, the New York Giants are donning their legacy uniforms against the Arizona Cardinals. New York wore these threads from 1980 to 1999. It was reintroduced in 2022, when the team brought back the navy helmet. Other design elements include classic numbers plus the red-and-blue trim on the jerseys and pants, similar to the uniforms of the 1980s and '90s. Written inside the collar is "Once a Giants, Always a Giant," the words of late owner Wellington Mara. 

The Carolina Panthers, meanwhile, will bring an all-black look to "Sunday Night Football" against the Detroit Lions. Carolina first debuted this all-black combination in 2022. 

The Dallas Cowboys are rocking navy blue alternates with silver pants against the Houston Texans, a look the team will wear only a handful of times each season. The Texans will wear liberty white jerseys with deep steel blue pants. It marks the same uniform matchup the Texans and Cowboys wore for Houston's first regular-season game as a franchise in 2002.

articles.headline: Spain's Víctor Muñoz on Liverpool switch: Premier League more physical than LaLiga
articles.description: Liverpool winger Víctor Muñoz has praised the "intensity" at the Premier League club since making the switch from LaLiga this summer, saying the change is "helping me grow" as a player.
articles.body:
Liverpool winger Víctor Muñoz has praised the "intensity" at the Premier League club since making the switch from LaLiga this summer, saying the change is "helping me grow" as a player.

Muñoz was the first arrival at Anfield under coach Andoni Iraola, signing a six-year contract after a €40 million ($45m) move from Osasuna which saw Liverpool beat Newcastle to his signature.

The wide forward was part of the Spain squad that won the World Cup this summer but was unable to take part in the tournament due to injury, and is back with the national team for this international break, featuring as a substitute against Croatia on Tuesday.

- Premier League 'dragged through the mud' by Man City case - Gary Neville

- Man City owners must sell due to 'shame of their guilt' - Jamie Carragher

- UK PM Burnham 'concerned' Man City's owners could sell club

"I definitely notice differences between LaLiga and the Premier League," Muñoz said in a news conference on Thursday, as Spain prepare to play Czechia in their latest Nations League game in Oviedo.

"LaLiga is a lot more tactical. The Premier League games are more physical. The intensity in training there is very high, you notice that difference. It's helping me grow."

Muñoz has made five Premier League appearances for Liverpool so far this season, scoring once.

The Real Madrid youth product enjoyed a breakout season at Osasuna in 2025-26 before his switch to England.

"Everything happening so fast means I don't have time to fully process it," he said on Thursday. "My family and I try to enjoy every moment... I'm in a good place right now."

Muñoz is now competing with Ballon d'Or contender Lamine Yamal for a place in the Spain team.

Yamal excelled against Croatia in Seville, scoring twice and providing an assist in a 4-1 win.

"I try to learn a lot from him," Muñoz said. "He's a good friend of mine, and we spend a lot of time together. Having that competition, seeing him train, it's a privilege for me."

articles.headline: Second Hull player flips car outside training ground - reports
articles.description: A second Hull player has been reported to have flipped his car in an accident close to the club's training ground in Cottingham.
articles.body:
A second Hull player has been reported to have flipped his car in an accident close to the club's training ground in Cottingham.

A photograph of a Mercedes car, which had rolled onto its side on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham, has been posted on social media.

In a similar incident three weeks ago, Hull midfielder Sorba Thomas escaped uninjured after rolling his car onto its roof on the same narrow residential street.

It has been reported that French summer signing Lucas Gourna-Douath was the driver in Thursday's accident.

Humberside Police said: "Officers and emergency services were called to reports of a single vehicle road traffic collision on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am this morning (Thursday, 1 October 2026).

"Thankfully, no one was injured as a result of the collision."

A brief Hull statement read: "Hull City is aware of images circulating on social media following a road traffic accident near the club's training ground and can confirm that no one was harmed in the incident."

- New Hull signing Sorba Thomas unhurt after flipping car near Premier League side's training ground

Thomas' Land Rover was pictured upside down on Millhouse Woods Lane after an incident on Sept. 11.

In response, local councillor Phil Redshaw said on Facebook that he had contacted the club earlier that week, urging them to remind players to drive with more care when approaching the training ground.

He said: "I only wrote to the club on Sunday, asking them to remind staff to drive with more care and attention when heading for the training ground!"

articles.headline: Fantasy playbook: NFL Week 4 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores
articles.description: An all-encompassing look at the matchups to exploit or avoid and lineup locks in fantasy, as well as projected scores for all NFL games.
articles.body:
Welcome to The Playbook for Week 4, which kicks off Thursday night with a game between the Steelers and Browns.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule as it stood before the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday. 

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are tracking Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah ahead of next summer, according to Bild. Los Blancos have scouted the 23-year-old England international as they look to add at least two defensive additions to their squad, following his solid displays in Germany since moving from Liverpool for €35 million in 2025, while previous suitors Arsenal are also monitoring developments.

The 23-year-old Greece international has impressed so far, with three clean sheets in five Premier League appearances following his £20 million summer move from Olympiakos.
